card.name: Linking words before harm or impairment
card.fires_on: Small linking words (in, to, could, that, are) and "Increased" right before a negative outcome is named, such as risk, damage, impairment or discrimination. It appears in warnings and adverse-effect text.

modes.label: Increase/decrease lead-ins
modes.description: The word increase or increased, or the word in after it, just before a risk or a rise in a body measure.
modes.example: - Anemia and fatigue if red blood cells counts are low -<< Increased>> risk of infection if white blood cell counts

modes.label: Links before harmful consequences
modes.description: A verb or linking word that leads into damage, impairment or harm.
modes.example: where an oil spill<< could>> cause irreversible damage to the pristine Great Bear

modes.label: Links before impairment
modes.description: The word to after drowsiness or similar, leading into impaired ability.
modes.example: as well as drowsiness sufficient<< to>> impair performance of potentially hazardous tasks, such

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words of inability, harm or destabilizing effects, and away from words of smooth or comfortable function.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a sentence where a bad effect or loss of ability is about to be named.
